cohort: Women within the postpartum period of 2 weeks to 6 months and aged 18 years or older in a rural area of Maharashtra, excluding those with prior psychiatric disorders, pre-existing chronic medical conditions, stillbirth, or neonatal death.
finding: The prevalence of postpartum depression was 13%, and several factors were associated with it, including older maternal age, higher maternal education, higher socioeconomic class, working mothers, higher birth order, cesarean delivery, antenatal complications, having a previous or current female child, history of abortion, marital conflict, domestic violence, poor relationship with in-laws, and lack of family involvement in child rearing.
mod_finding: Cesarean delivery was associated with postpartum depression (79%, p=0.002).
